:::{#def-correlation}
#### Correlation

The **correlation** of two [random variables](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) $X$ and $Y$
with finite, positive [variances](#def-variance)
is their [covariance](#def-cov)
divided by the product of their [standard deviations](#def-sd):

$$\Cor{X,Y} \eqdef \frac{\Cov{X,Y}}{\SD{X}\,\SD{Y}}$$

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

Dividing by the [standard deviations](#def-sd) removes the units of $X$ and $Y$.
This [population correlation](#def-correlation) is a property of a [joint distribution](random-variables.qmd#def-joint-distribution);
the sample (Pearson) correlation coefficient computed from data estimates it.

:::
